title: telemetry-driven-slo-decision-inspector-and-graceful-unwind-hotpatch
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: During a recent incident (INC-2026-02-high-kv-pressure) we observed aggressive tenant eviction and immediate circuit flips for tenants with marginal SLO violations. Root cause analysis showed a lack of machine-readable justification attached to SLO enforcement decisions and a hard circuit unwind that did not account for transient KV pressure spikes. Motivation: Provide operators and SREs better observability into why a request was shed or a tenant downgraded, and soften abrupt rejections with a short-lived graceful-unwind path that gives recovery-friendly signals and reduces customer-facing errors. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a SLO Decision Inspector (runtime telemetry component) that emits structured rationale for shedding/circuit transitions, and 2) a Graceful Unwind polyfill that implements a short, probabilistic slow-path acceptance window instead of a binary reject during short-lived SLO overages. Summary of changes: - runtime/inspector: add decision_inspector.go which produces compact decision records (json-lines) with reason, inputs (slo_score, kv_pressure, inflight, tenant_weight), and suggested_action (shed/queue-accept/defer). Records are emitted to the local telemetry buffer and to the decision-audit log stream when configured. - runtime/shedder: introduce graceful_unwind.go which implements a tokenized slow-path that accepts a small fraction of requests for a configurable window when SLO breach is detected. Slow-path uses exponential backoff on acceptance rate when errors persist. - orchestration: small feature flag (feature.slo_decision_inspector) and runtime config knobs (graceful_unwind.window_ms, graceful_unwind.initial_accept_pct, graceful_unwind.cooldown_ms) added to config schema and console defaults. - tests: unit + integration tests that simulate KV pressure spikes and assert no customer-visible 5xx increase while keeping SLO error budget accounting intact. - docs: new troubleshooting section in docs/observability/slo-decision-inspector.md with sample queries and Kibana dashboards. Implementation notes: - Decision records are intentionally compact and redact tenant identifiers by default; when tenant opt-in is present (via org-config) full context can be emitted to the audit stream. - The graceful unwind is conservative by default: 5% initial acceptance for 5s window, halving acceptance on each error, and full revert to normal policy after cooldown. - We preserved existing metric names; new metrics: slo_decision.recorded, graceful_unwind.accepted, graceful_unwind.rejected, graceful_unwind.window_entered. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind feature.slo_decision_inspector and gradual rollout via console controls. - Step 1: enable telemetry recording only in staging for 24h, validate record volume. - Step 2: enable decision-audit stream for a small set of tenants (canary) and validate operator dashboards. - Step 3: enable graceful_unwind at 1% of clusters, monitor 5xx, latency, and slo_decision.* metrics. - Backout: revert feature flag or set initial_accept_pct to 0 to disable graceful path immediately. - Ops runbook entries added (docs link). Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests against kv-pressure harness - [x] docs updated - [x] feature flag and config validated - [x] telemetry (record sampling) implemented - [x] runbook and rollback steps documented Commits summary: - Add decision inspector and serializers - Implement graceful unwind slow-path and integrate with shedder - Add feature flag, config, and console defaults - Tests and telemetry dashboards - Docs and runbook Changes (high level): - src/runtime/inspector/decision_inspector.go - src/runtime/shedder/graceful_unwind.go - src/config/feature_flags.go (add flag) - src/config/graceful_unwind.yaml (defaults) - telemetry/dashboards/slo_decision_inspector.json - tests/integration/kv_pressure_unwind_test.go - docs/observability/slo-decision-inspector.md Review notes: reviewers asked for a tight retention policy for decision records and assurance that no PII leaks into the default stream. I added redaction by default and a per-tenant opt-in documented in the runbook. CI: full unit suite and integration harness were run on linux-amd64 and linux-arm64; small lint fixes applied after initial run. Expected impact: reduce noisy tenant evictions, surface actionable telemetry for SRE/engineers, and lower customer-visible 5xx at marginal slowdowns without increasing overall SLO cost materially.
